subject: ACME bake-off: discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: ACME bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call + proposed next steps so we're all aligned. High level pain & goals we heard:

- Pain points:
  - Unpredictable latency and cost from current setup (mix of vLLM on prem + managed TGI endpoints) causing inconsistent user experience for interactive features.
  - Operational overhead: rollouts, model variant testing, and KV cache state are handled ad-hoc.
  - Security/compliance: audit logs and tenant isolation requirements for PII-sensitive prompts.

- Current stack you described:
  - Inference: vLLM for on-prem, TGI-managed endpoints on cloud for burst.
  - Orchestration: homegrown router, S3 for artifacts, GA4 for usage metrics.
  - Team: 2 infra engineers, 1 ML engineer dedicated to serving.

- Success criteria for bake-off (what will make this a win for Acme):
  1) Latency: p50 < 100 ms, p95 < 300 ms for typical 256-token chat requests at expected concurrency.
  2) Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent chatting sessions with graceful degradation.
  3) Cost: demonstrable reduction in $/1M tokens vs current managed endpoints (target 20% lower).
  4) Quality parity: no regression on your accuracy/QA prompt set (we'll run your evals).
  5) Controls: per-tenant audit logs and ability to pin model versions.

What we'll run in the bake-off:
- Benchmarks: latency (p50/p95), throughput (TPS), cost estimates, and quality evals on your prompt set.
- Comparison targets: your vLLM on-prem baseline, current TGI managed endpoints, and Redwood hosted/Dedicated endpoints.
- Acceptance: we'll measure against the success criteria above and produce a short scoreboard.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a bake-off criteria workbook (attached) — please confirm fields and any additional KPIs.
2) If you're OK, please share a representative sample prompt set (anonymized) and a short traffic profile (qps distribution, typical token lengths).
3) Rishi will reach out to coordinate the technical requirements (SSH/credentials for test connector or a small proxy dataset transfer).
4) Let's schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to finalize the test window and who owns runbooks.

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_criteria.xlsx (bake-off metrics + template), redwood-pricing-qual.pdf (high-level pricing & qualifying questions).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priorities: Latency and quality are top priority, cost is secondary but still important. We cannot exceed p95 > 400 ms for synchronous chat flows.
- Acceptance criteria additions:
  - Determinism: for the exact model+seed we need repeatable outputs for a subset of prompts used in A/B evaluation.
  - Cold-start behavior: 95% of requests should hit prefix/KV cache at steady state.

On benchmarks:
- For comparison please include the following targets in the report:
  1) vLLM (our on-prem baseline) — we can provide a runbook and a small VM for remote tests.
  2) TGI-managed endpoints (current managed provider) — we'll share recent logs (anonymized) to help replicate request patterns.
  3) Redwood hosted/Dedicated — include both a hosted API run and a Dedicated pool configuration estimate.

We will: share an anonymized prompt set and a short traffic profile by EOD tomorrow. Can you confirm the inputs you need in the prompt set (format, fields)? Also confirm whether the bake-off requires any contract/legal paperwork (NDA or DPA) before we share PII-containing prompts — Procurement is CC'd.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Product, Acme.ai
jordan.lee@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Great — appreciate the priorities and the added acceptance items. Quick answers: 

- Prompt set format: JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected_metadata (optional), anonymized_user_id. If you have multiple turn contexts, include a "context" array per item. The sample we attached (acme_sample_prompts.jsonl) should be fine.
- Benchmarks we'll produce: p50/p95 latency (ms) across token lengths (64/128/256), tokens/sec throughput under target concurrency, end-to-end cost estimate $/1M tokens for each target, and evaluation scores on your QA set (we'll report BLEU/Exact-match/F1 depending on task).
- Determinism note: we'll include a deterministic run (seeded) for the subset you flagged and indicate any sampling/temperature differences.
- Cold-start behavior: we'll report cache hit rates and time-to-warm metrics.
- Legal: We can execute a short DPA/NDA if required — happy to loop in our contracts team. No vendor-level contract is required to run an initial bake-off, but if you need DPA before sharing PII we can fast-track.

Next steps:
1) Rishi will send a small technical checklist (networking, dataset upload options, credentials for any test connectors).
2) Please upload the anonymized prompt set to the Drive link in the workbook or send to rishi via secure upload.
3) Proposed kickoff: Wed 13 May 2026 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for you?

I've attached an updated bake-off workbook with suggested KPIs and a sample scoreboard.

Best,
Marissa
